title: Fracturing-aware Curvilinear ILT via Circular E-beam Mask Writer
problem: Curvilinear masks from inverse lithography technology must be fractured into rectangles for traditional mask writers, requiring prohibitively expensive write times and high shot counts. A circular E-beam mask writer offering variable-radius circle writing per shot provides an alternative fracturing strategy.
motivation: Reducing mask write time and manufacturing cost while preserving the optimal process windows achieved by curvilinear mask designs is essential for semiconductor cost reduction.
method: Two methods are developed: (1) a rule-based converter that transforms pixel-based masks from existing ILT into circle-based masks, and (2) a constrained ILT optimizer that directly generates circle-based masks by integrating circular geometry constraints into the optimization process. Both exploit the variable-radius circular shot capability of the novel E-beam mask writer.
key_novelty: Fracturing-aware mask optimization for circular E-beam writers, eliminating rectangle-based fracturing overhead through native circular geometry representation.
contributions: Rule-based conversion method for pixel-to-circle mask transformation compatible with existing ILT
Direct circular-constrained optimization for native circle-based mask generation
Significant reduction in shot count versus traditional rectangle fracturing
Process window preservation validation for both conversion approaches

metrics.speedup: reduced shot count and write time

primary_theme: Circular fracturing for mask write optimization
